text.Cover Subtitle: Architecture update for the platform review board

text.Agenda List:
01  Why we re-architected the inference stack after the 2025 outages
02  New runtime design: gateway, compiled kernels and the device scheduler
03  Latency and cost results from the six-week production pilot
04  Rollout plan, risks and what we need from the review board

text.Content Title: The new runtime has three layers
text.Column Body 1:
Routes every request by model version, device class and tenant, and applies per-tenant quotas before work reaches the fleet.
Adds canary and shadow traffic so new models can be validated against live requests without user impact.
text.Column Body 2:
Ahead-of-time compiled kernels for the eight most common operator patterns remove the JIT warm-up that dominated cold-start latency.
Kernels are cached per device family.
text.Column Body 3:
A device-aware scheduler packs requests onto accelerators using measured, not nominal, throughput.
It drains nodes gracefully during upgrades.

text.Metric Points:
p99 latency fell from 410 ms to 190 ms across all regions during the pilot
Cold starts are now under 2 seconds for 95% of model loads
Cost per thousand requests dropped by 38% at the same traffic volume
